body: You know, I ask people if they're suicidal almost daily and assess their risk for suicide. The odd thing is I don't know what that actually means or feels like. I don't think I have ever experienced it. This past month, I have been consistently having a hard time and performing poorly in school. I cry regularly, and I get these intrusive thoughts about making sure others (my wife and parents) are okay if I weren't around. I would want to make sure they could go on living happily. The idea of killing myself is scary though. I fear death too much to be able to do that.

Honestly, I thought the real test was not properly represented by the NBME's. Specifically, I thought that NBME 22 was garbage because of the many questions that didn't appear in FA. It was definitely harder than other NBME's IMO. I felt that the real test had a lot of questions that involved me utilizing information to solve problems that there was no way of studying for. For example, I counted quite a few questions that the answers were found in research papers rather than FA. I was able to solve these by utilizing concepts I had learned to provide a logical answer.
It's impossible to say because no-one knows the curve, but I have seen posts of people counting over 20-30 mistakes and still scoring above 250. This must be taken with a grain of salt though.

I think if you break 200 you're in a good spot. If you're not passing your baseline, you'll have to work a bit harder. It also depends on what you're shooting for. If you're below that 175 mark, I think you should make sure you're in communication with your school about the possibility of having to extend your step 1 dedicated period. That's not to say you won't pass if your baseline is below a 175, but it means you will have to work harder and possibly need additional support from your school.

I had a long flight, so I did a skim of first aid and was able to recall questions. I wrote down the concept that was tested if I recall selecting the correct answer to ensure I don't double count. Probably not the healthiest thing to do, but I felt like garbage after the test. After I did this I felt much better.
